## What the kanban proves (the re-diagnosis)

`managent dispatch` is NOT the chokepoint: only 21 of 69 kanban rows (30%) carry a dispatched event; the operator pastes prompts directly and no dispatch record exists for the rest, so a dispatch-time guard could not have refused anything. A claim-time guard fires too late: consoles do the work FIRST and record claim+done together at the end. Of the 54 closed rows carrying both timestamps, 9 (16.7%) have claim within 10 seconds of done — the claim-at-close pattern — including the three duplicates the brief names:

  T336  claimed 2026-08-03T23:38:04Z done 23:38:05Z  (1s)
  T349  claimed 2026-08-04T15:14:25Z done 15:14:25Z  (0s)
  T367  claimed 2026-08-05T12:15:04Z done 12:15:04Z  (0s)
  T371  claimed 2026-08-05T13:08:35Z done 13:08:35Z  (0s)
  T376  claimed 2026-08-05T13:28:50Z done 13:28:51Z  (1s)
  T380  claimed 2026-08-05T21:34:36Z done 21:34:36Z  (0s)
  T384  claimed 2026-08-05T22:49:47Z done 22:49:55Z  (8s)
  T388  claimed 2026-08-06T01:22:10Z done 01:22:10Z  (0s)
  T370  claimed 2026-08-06T01:34:51Z done 01:34:58Z  (7s)

Five are same-second. T389 (the post-close-edit duplicate) is NOT in this list — its claim gap is 1668s; its hazard was the second console editing a committed deliverable AFTER close, which the done gate cannot see and the new audit check catches. The two mechanisms are complementary: the done gate refuses claim-at-close, the audit reports post-close/unclaimed edits.

## What changed in src/managent/main.zig

1. cmdDone claim-at-close gate (CLAIM_TO_DONE_REFUSE_SECS = 10): a done whose claimed timestamp is within 10s of now is REJECTED before any store mutation, with the claim timestamp and gap named and a pointer at the correct flow (claim at the START of the work). --force closes loudly ('FORCED: ... claim-at-close acknowledged'). Placement: right after the in_progress status check, before attribution/deliverable/acceptance — the refusal never mutates the store. Age computed with a new nowUnix() helper + the existing ageSecFromTs (already used by resume/liveness); a negative gap (claimed in the future) is also refused.
2. cmdDispatch second-dispatch refusal: a row with dispatched already set is REJECTED naming the previous holder (dispatched_to) and timestamp; --force re-dispatches loudly (the T379 genuinely-dead-console shape). Previously a second dispatch silently overwrote dispatched_to.
3. cmdClaim refusal hardened: the row-level refusal for in_progress already existed; it now names the holder AND the claim timestamp, and no longer prints a phantom '.<attempt>' suffix — claim_count is now bumped only on a claim that persists (moved into the two success branches, before writeStateLocked), so a refused claim's message names the holder as the store has it. Verified: 'ALREADY CLAIMED ... by deepseek-v4-pro/TB since 2026-08-01T00:00:01Z' with no TB.2 suffix (regression control d).
4. cmdAudit dirty-deliverable check (T390): a done or dispatchable row whose bundle deliverables= paths are dirty in the working tree is a FIX finding — the T389 shape (second console editing a committed deliverable of an already-closed row) and the T367 shape (worked without ever claiming). Refinements so the live kanban does not go permanently red:
   - kanban-store files (tasks.json / directives.jsonl / heartbeat.jsonl) are excluded — managent itself writes them on every claim/dispatch/close, so their dirtiness is the live kanban's normal state, not unclaimed work (same exclusion treeDirty already applies);
   - done rows closed as blocked/abandoned are exempt — the done gate never required deliverables for those verdicts (T361/T379/T349 closed with no work at all), so their never-created paths are noise, not hazard;
   - dispatchable rows are filtered by exists-on-disk: a not-yet-created deliverable is normal for an unstarted row; only an existing-and-dirty file is evidence of work.

## Regression controls (tools/regression-duplicate-dispatch.sh, wired into zig build test)

All 12 PASS against the deployed binary: a fresh dispatch succeeds; b second dispatch refuses naming the holder; c --force re-dispatch succeeds loudly; d claim on a claimed row refuses with holder+timestamp and no phantom suffix; e claim-then-done within seconds refuses, --force closes loudly; f normally-claimed row closes without --force; g audit clean on done row with committed deliverable, g2 FIX on the same row dirtied; h audit silent on dispatchable row whose deliverable is not yet created (negative control — unstarted rows are not flagged), h2 FIX on an existing dirty deliverable; i live kanban byte-identical.

## Incidental (pre-existing, required by the contract change)

regression-managent-integrity.sh checks 6/7/8 claimed a task and closed it in the same breath — exactly the pattern the new done gate refuses. Updated those four done calls to pass --force so the checks keep testing verdict plumbing rather than the new gate. The script is T204's deliverable; the update is the same 'incidental' category T350 applied to regression-git-commit-mine-hook.sh. Full suite: all managent regressions PASS in-suite (duplicate-dispatch, done-two-phase 7/7, integrity 19/19, lock, done-git, resume, standing, task-identity, smoke PASS); the only suite failures are the documented pre-existing engine-module reds (vb_bellman_4x4 applyMove panic, qa023_brute_2x2 smoke ABRT x4, differential/calibration I9/A2/I4/A1) — none import src/managent/main.zig.

## Live-tree audit state

With the refinements above, `bin/managent audit` on the live tree reports exactly the honest set: every FIX it currently emits for done/dispatchable rows names src/managent/main.zig, build.zig or tools/regression-managent-integrity.sh — i.e. THIS change's own uncommitted edits (T317/T319/T322/T350 done, T353/T364 dispatchable) — and the pre-existing T365 holds='docs/audits' finding. All clear on commit. This is the intended sharpness: an unclaimed edit to a deliverable of a closed row is exactly what the check exists to surface.
